Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_symbols¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_symbols(const Note& other) const

Math-Symbol Containment Score Between Two Notes¶

overlap_symbols(other) scores each cell pair by the overlap coefficient of their math-symbol sets and returns a shape-preserving Float64 Note of native scores. It is the math-symbol containment member of the set-similarity family; see also jaccard_symbols and intersect_symbols.

How the score is computed¶

A math symbol is a TeX-style command (\ plus ASCII letters, e.g. \alpha, \sum) or a single operator character from + - * / = < > ^. Commands keep their backslash and are compared case-sensitively. Symbols are deduplicated into sets A and B; the score is |A ∩ B| / min(|A|, |B|), in [0, 1], symmetric — 1.0 when the smaller symbol set is contained in the larger.

A cell with none of \ + - * / = < > ^ has an empty set. Both sets empty → 1.0; one empty and one not → 0.0. The default printer shows up to six decimals, trailing zeros trimmed.

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Bytes-mode input raises Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_symbols requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs); a numel mismatch raises Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_symbols expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Smaller Expression Contained In The Larger¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\sum + \\int"})
                 .nlp().overlap_symbols(pluss::make_note({"\\sum + \\int - \\lim = 0"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, dtype=Float64)
[1]

{\sum, +, \int} is a subset of {\sum, +, \int, -, \lim, =} → 1.0.
